statute_title: Driving Under the Influence / Driving While Ability Impaired
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle or vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol or drugs (DUI) with BAC .08+
Or while ability impaired (DWAI) with BAC .05-.079
Or while under the influence of any drug or combination of drug and alcohol
enhancements: BAC .15 or higher (Persistent Drunk Driver designation)
Child under 16 in vehicle (Class 6 Felony child abuse)
Prior vehicular assault or vehicular homicide
notes: Colorado distinguishes between DUI (.08+ BAC) and DWAI (.05-.079 BAC). Fourth DUI is a Class 4 Felony under § 42-4-1301(1)(a). Express consent law under § 42-4-1301.1. Persistent Drunk Driver designation triggers enhanced requirements.

elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or both
BAC .08 or higher, or substantially incapable of safely operating a vehicle
No prior DUI/DWAI convictions
mandatory_minimum: 5 days imprisonment (may be suspended if completes Level II alcohol education)
notes: Eligible for deferred judgment on first offense. 9-month license revocation. Community service of 48-96 hours. Level II alcohol education required.

elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle
While under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or both
One or more prior DUI/DWAI convictions
mandatory_minimum: 10 days and 48 hours community service (second); 60 days and 48 hours community service (third); 90 days to 6 years (fourth+)
notes: Fourth DUI became a Class 4 Felony in 2015 (HB 15-1043). Two-year license revocation for second offense. Ignition interlock required for repeat offenders.

offense_class: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
penalty_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
fine_max: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle
While under the influence of one or more drugs
Or under the combined influence of alcohol and drugs
Such that the defendant was substantially incapable of safely operating a vehicle
mandatory_minimum: Same as alcohol DUI by offense count
enhancements: THC blood level 5 ng/mL or higher (permissible inference of impairment)
Combined influence of alcohol and drugs
notes: Colorado has a permissible inference of impairment at 5 ng/mL THC in blood. No per se limit — jury may still consider all evidence. Same penalty structure as alcohol DUI.

elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle
In a manner that indicated a wanton or willful disregard for the safety of persons or property
notes: Common plea-down from DUI. 8 points on driving record. Separate from careless driving (§ 42-4-1402, Class 2 Misdemeanor Traffic Offense).

statute_title: Duty to Stop at Scene — Accident Involving Death or Injury
offense_class: Class 3 Felony (death); Class 4 Felony (serious bodily injury); Class 1 Misdemeanor Traffic Offense (injury); Class 2 Misdemeanor Traffic Offense (property damage under § 42-4-1602)
penalty_max: 12 years (death); 6 years (serious bodily injury); 1 year (injury); 90 days (property)
elements: Defendant was the driver of a vehicle involved in an accident
Accident resulted in injury, death, or property damage
Defendant failed to stop at the scene
Defendant failed to provide identification and render reasonable assistance
notes: Leaving the scene involving death is a Class 3 Felony. Mandatory revocation of driver's license.

elements: Defendant operated or drove a motor vehicle
In a reckless manner or while under the influence of alcohol or drugs
Proximately caused the death of another person
notes: DUI-related vehicular homicide is a Class 3 Felony. Reckless driving-related is a Class 4 Felony. Mandatory license revocation.

elements: Defendant operated or drove a motor vehicle
In a reckless manner
Proximately caused the death of another person
notes: Colorado does not use 'vehicular manslaughter' terminology but the reckless driving variant of vehicular homicide serves this function.

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor Traffic Offense (basic); Class 1 Misdemeanor Traffic Offense (alcohol-related restraint)
elements: Defendant drove a motor vehicle on a public road
Defendant's license was under restraint, suspended, or revoked
Defendant had knowledge of the restraint
enhancements: Driving under restraint for alcohol-related offense (Class 1 Misdemeanor Traffic Offense)
notes: Colorado uses 'driving under restraint' rather than 'driving on suspended.' Alcohol-related restraint carries enhanced penalties.

elements: Defendant while operating a motor vehicle
Knowingly fled or attempted to elude a peace officer
After being given a visual or audible signal to stop
enhancements: Creating a substantial risk of serious bodily injury or death (Class 4 Felony)
notes: Vehicular eluding is always a felony. If conduct creates a substantial risk of serious bodily injury or death, elevated to Class 4 Felony.

statute_title: Unlawful Possession of a Controlled Substance
offense_class: Level 1 Drug Misdemeanor (4g or less of Schedule I/II); Level 4 Drug Felony (over 4g of Schedule I/II)
penalty_max: 180 days (Level 1 Drug Misdemeanor); 1 year (Level 4 Drug Felony)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a controlled substance
Substance is listed in Colorado Controlled Substances Act schedules
Possession was without a valid prescription or lawful authority
enhancements: Over 4g of Schedule I/II (Level 4 Drug Felony)
notes: Colorado significantly reformed drug possession laws in 2019 (HB 19-1263). Possession of 4g or less of Schedule I/II is a Level 1 Drug Misdemeanor. Marijuana regulated separately under Amendment 64.

offense_class: Drug Petty Offense (1-2 oz. over limit); Level 2 Drug Misdemeanor (2-6 oz. over limit); Level 1 Drug Misdemeanor (6-12 oz. over limit)
penalty_max: No incarceration (petty offense); 120 days (Level 2 DM); 180 days (Level 1 DM)
elements: Defendant possessed marijuana
In excess of the legal limit for personal use (over 2 oz.)
Or was under 21 years of age possessing any amount
notes: Colorado legalized recreational marijuana in 2012 (Amendment 64). Adults 21+ may possess up to 2 oz. Possession over the legal limit is still criminal. Medical patients may possess higher amounts.

offense_class: Level 1 Drug Misdemeanor (4g or less); Level 4 Drug Felony (over 4g)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed cocaine
Cocaine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Under 2019 reform, possession of 4g or less of cocaine is a Level 1 Drug Misdemeanor. Treatment-focused approach emphasized.

offense_class: Level 1 Drug Misdemeanor (4g or less); Level 4 Drug Felony (over 4g)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed methamphetamine
Methamphetamine is a Schedule II controlled substance
Possession was without lawful authority
notes: Same 4g threshold as cocaine. Manufacturing meth is a separate Level 1 Drug Felony under § 18-18-405.

statute_title: Drug Trafficking — Distribution of Large Quantities
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured, dispensed, sold, or distributed
Or possessed with intent to manufacture, dispense, sell, or distribute
A controlled substance in a quantity exceeding trafficking thresholds
notes: Level 1 Drug Felony carries 8-32 years. Thresholds vary by substance. Includes large-scale distribution operations.

statute_title: Unlawful Distribution, Manufacturing, Dispensing, or Sale
offense_class: Level 2 Drug Felony (Schedule I/II); Level 3 Drug Felony (Schedule III/IV); Level 1 Drug Misdemeanor (Schedule V)
penalty_max: 8 years (Level 2 DF); 4 years (Level 3 DF); 180 days (Level 1 DM)
elements: Defendant knowingly distributed, sold, or dispensed a controlled substance
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Distribution to a minor (§ 18-18-407, enhanced one level)
notes: Colorado uses 'distribution' and 'sale.' Enhancement for distribution to minors or near schools.

offense_class: Level 1 Drug Felony (meth/fentanyl); Level 2 Drug Felony (other Schedule I/II)
elements: Defendant knowingly manufactured, produced, or processed a controlled substance
Or possessed precursors with intent to manufacture
Without lawful authority
enhancements: Manufacturing methamphetamine or fentanyl (Level 1 Drug Felony)
notes: Manufacturing meth or fentanyl is a Level 1 Drug Felony with 8-32 years. Other manufacturing is Level 2. Colorado has seen a significant fentanyl crisis driving legislative changes.

elements: Defendant possessed drug paraphernalia
With intent to use it for a controlled substance
enhancements: Delivery of paraphernalia to a minor (Level 2 Drug Misdemeanor)
notes: Simple possession of paraphernalia is a petty offense with only a fine. Delivery to a minor is more serious. Marijuana paraphernalia is legal for adults 21+.

offense_class: Level 2 Drug Felony (Schedule I/II); Level 3 Drug Felony (Schedule III/IV)
elements: Defendant possessed a controlled substance
With intent to manufacture, dispense, sell, or distribute
Without lawful authority
notes: Intent can be inferred from quantity, packaging, scales, cash, and other circumstantial evidence.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
After deliberation and with the intent to cause the death
Or caused death during the commission of certain enumerated felonies (felony murder)
mandatory_minimum: Life imprisonment without the possibility of parole
enhancements: Felony murder (during kidnapping, sexual assault, arson, robbery, burglary, escape)
Murder of a peace officer or firefighter
notes: Colorado abolished the death penalty in 2020 (SB 20-100). Maximum sentence is life without parole. Felony murder is first-degree murder.

elements: Defendant knowingly caused the death of another person
But without deliberation
enhancements: Extreme indifference to human life (Class 2 Felony)
notes: Second-degree murder covers intentional killings without premeditation and depraved-heart killings. Colorado has no separate depraved-heart murder statute.

elements: Defendant recklessly caused the death of another person
Or the defendant intentionally caused the death under a sudden heat of passion provoked by the victim
notes: Colorado's manslaughter statute covers both reckless killings and heat-of-passion killings. Heat of passion is an affirmative defense to murder, reducing it to manslaughter.

elements: Defendant caused the death of another person
By conduct amounting to criminal negligence
Defendant failed to perceive a substantial and unjustifiable risk
notes: Colorado uses 'criminally negligent homicide' rather than 'involuntary manslaughter.' Class 5 Felony. Lower culpability than manslaughter.

elements: Defendant with intent to cause serious bodily injury caused serious bodily injury to another person
By means of a deadly weapon
Or caused serious bodily injury under circumstances manifesting extreme indifference to the value of human life
enhancements: Against a peace officer or firefighter
notes: First-degree assault is a Class 3 Felony. If classified as a crime of violence, the court must sentence to DOC (no probation). Extraordinary risk crimes add additional time.

elements: Defendant knowingly or recklessly caused bodily injury to another person
Or with criminal negligence caused bodily injury by means of a deadly weapon
notes: Third-degree assault is the base assault offense. Class 1 Misdemeanor with up to 18 months (extraordinary risk offense).

statute_title: Assault in the Third Degree (Battery equivalent)
elements: Defendant knowingly or recklessly caused bodily injury to another person
notes: Colorado merged assault and battery into the assault statutes. There is no separate battery offense.

elements: Defendant knowingly took anything of value from the person or presence of another
By the use of force, threats, or intimidation
notes: Base robbery is a Class 4 Felony. Aggravated robbery (§ 18-4-302) involving a deadly weapon or serious bodily injury is a Class 3 Felony with mandatory DOC sentence.

elements: Defendant committed a robbery
While armed with a deadly weapon
Or while representing by words or conduct to be armed
Or serious bodily injury was inflicted
notes: Aggravated robbery is a crime of violence — mandatory DOC sentence. One of the most commonly charged violent felonies in Colorado.

offense_class: Class 1 Felony (if victim not released alive); Class 2 Felony (otherwise)
elements: Defendant knowingly seized and carried another person from one place to another
Or enticed or persuaded another to go from one place to another
Without consent and without lawful justification
With intent to hold for ransom, use as a shield or hostage, rob, facilitate a felony, or inflict injury
notes: First-degree kidnapping where victim is not released alive is a Class 1 Felony (life without parole). Second-degree kidnapping (§ 18-3-302) is a Class 2 Felony.

elements: Defendant knowingly set fire to, burned, or caused to be burned
Or aided, counseled, or procured the burning of
Any building or occupied structure
notes: First-degree arson targets buildings and occupied structures. Second-degree (§ 18-4-103) covers other property. Third-degree (§ 18-4-104) covers lesser property damage. Fourth-degree (§ 18-4-105) is a misdemeanor.

statute_title: Criminal Attempt — Murder in the First Degree
elements: Defendant intended to cause the death of another person
Defendant engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward the commission of murder
notes: Attempted murder of the first degree is a Class 2 Felony. Crime of violence sentencing may apply.

statute_title: Assault in the First Degree — With Deadly Weapon
elements: Defendant with intent to cause serious bodily injury
Caused serious bodily injury to another person
By means of a deadly weapon
notes: Crime of violence — mandatory DOC sentence. Deadly weapon includes firearm, knife, or any instrument capable of causing death or serious bodily injury.

offense_class: Class 2 Felony ($1,000,000+); Class 3 Felony ($100,000-$1,000,000); Class 4 Felony ($20,000-$100,000); Class 5 Felony ($5,000-$20,000); Class 6 Felony ($2,000-$5,000); Class 1 Misdemeanor ($750-$2,000); Class 2 Misdemeanor ($300-$750); Petty Offense (under $300)
penalty_max: 24 years (Class 2); 12 years (Class 3); 6 years (Class 4); 3 years (Class 5); 18 months (Class 6); 18 months (Class 1 Misd.); 120 days (Class 2 Misd.)
elements: Defendant knowingly obtained, retained, or exercised control over anything of value of another
Without authorization or by threat or deception
With the intent to permanently deprive the owner
enhancements: Theft from an at-risk person (enhanced one class)
notes: Colorado has a detailed value-based classification system for theft. Theft from an at-risk adult or juvenile is enhanced by one class.

elements: Defendant knowingly obtained, retained, or exercised control over property
Value exceeds $20,000
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Colorado uses graduated felony classes rather than 'grand theft' terminology. $20,000+ is the common felony threshold for significant theft.

elements: Defendant knowingly obtained, retained, or exercised control over property
Value is under $300
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Under $300 is a petty offense with only a fine. $300-$750 is a Class 2 Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Same as theft by value tier
penalty_max: Same as theft by value tier
fine_max: Same as theft by value tier
elements: Defendant concealed, removed, or altered merchandise
Of a retail establishment
With intent to deprive the merchant of value without paying
enhancements: Use of booster bags or devices
notes: Colorado enacted organized retail theft provisions. Penalties follow the standard theft value tiers.

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor (third degree); Class 4 Felony (second degree); Class 3 Felony (first degree)
elements: Defendant knowingly broke into or entered an enclosed area or building
With the intent to commit a crime therein
notes: Third degree covers enclosed areas (vaults, safes, coin machines). Second degree (§ 18-4-202) covers buildings/occupied structures. First degree (§ 18-4-201) covers dwellings.

elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained unlawfully
In a building or occupied structure that was a dwelling
With the intent to commit a crime therein
enhancements: Menacing or assault during burglary (crime of violence)
notes: First-degree burglary is a crime of violence if the defendant assaults or menaces anyone during the burglary. Mandatory DOC sentence in that case.

offense_class: Class 5 Felony (first degree); Class 1 Misdemeanor (second degree, under $2,000 value)
elements: Defendant knowingly obtained or exercised control over a motor vehicle of another
Without authorization
With intent to permanently deprive the owner or temporarily deprive the owner of possession
enhancements: Use in commission of another crime
notes: Colorado has a specific motor vehicle theft statute. First degree covers most MVT. Second degree covers joyriding or low-value vehicles.

offense_class: Same class structure as theft based on value
penalty_max: Same as theft by value tier
fine_max: Same as theft by value tier
elements: Defendant received, retained, loaned money by pawn or pledge, or otherwise disposed of anything of value
Knowing or believing it was stolen
notes: Colorado combines receiving stolen property under the general theft statute. Same value-based classification system.

offense_class: Class 2 Felony ($1,000,000+); down to Petty Offense (under $300) — same tiers as theft
penalty_max: Varies by damage amount (same tiers as theft)
elements: Defendant knowingly damaged the real or personal property of another
Without the owner's consent
enhancements: Damage to utility or communication property
notes: Colorado uses 'criminal mischief.' Same value-tier classification as theft. Under $300 is a petty offense; over $1,000,000 is a Class 2 Felony.

offense_class: Class 5 Felony (dwelling); Class 2 Misdemeanor (other premises under § 18-4-503); Class 3 Misdemeanor (motor vehicle under § 18-4-504)
elements: Defendant knowingly and unlawfully entered or remained
In a dwelling of another (first degree)
Or other premises or enclosed area (second/third degree)
notes: First-degree trespass of a dwelling is a Class 5 Felony. Second-degree (other premises) is a Class 2 Misdemeanor. Third-degree (motor vehicle) is a Class 3 Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Varies by damage amount (same tiers as theft)
elements: Defendant knowingly damaged the real or personal property of another
Without the owner's consent
enhancements: Damage by means of explosive or fire
Damage to utility or communication property
notes: Classification follows the same value thresholds as theft. Damage to a fire station or school may carry enhanced penalties.

offense_class: Sentence enhancer — not a standalone offense; enhances underlying offense
elements: Defendant committed an act of violence or threatened act of violence
Against a person with whom the defendant is or has been in an intimate relationship
Intimate relationship includes spouse, former spouse, unmarried couple, or persons who are or have been in a dating relationship
mandatory_minimum: Mandatory arrest; mandatory 36-week domestic violence treatment program upon conviction
notes: Domestic violence is a sentence enhancer in Colorado, not a standalone crime. It attaches to the underlying offense (assault, harassment, menacing, etc.) and triggers mandatory treatment, no deferred judgments, and mandatory protection order.

elements: Defendant knowingly or recklessly caused bodily injury to an intimate partner
Or with criminal negligence caused bodily injury by means of a deadly weapon to an intimate partner
enhancements: Serious bodily injury (elevated to first-degree assault)
notes: Assault 3 with DV enhancer is the most common domestic battery charge. No deferred judgment allowed for domestic violence offenses.

offense_class: Class 2 Felony (knowingly causing death); Class 3 Felony (knowingly causing serious bodily injury); Class 2 Misdemeanor (negligent treatment creating risk)
elements: Defendant caused injury to a child's life or health
Or placed a child in a situation that posed a threat to the child's life or health
Knowingly, recklessly, or with criminal negligence
notes: Colorado's child abuse statute is very broad, covering physical abuse, negligent supervision, and exposure to harmful situations. Ranges from misdemeanor to Class 2 Felony.

offense_class: Class 3 Felony (serious bodily injury); Class 2 Felony (death)
elements: Defendant knowingly or recklessly caused injury to a child's life or health
Resulted in serious bodily injury or death
notes: Knowing or reckless child abuse resulting in serious injury or death is one of the most seriously punished offenses in Colorado.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (first); Class 5 Felony (second within 7 years); Class 4 Felony (third within 7 years)
elements: A valid protection order was in effect
Defendant had notice of the protection order
Defendant knowingly violated a condition of the order
notes: Escalating penalties. First violation is Class 1 Misdemeanor. Second within 7 years is Class 5 Felony. Third within 7 years is Class 4 Felony.

offense_class: Class 5 Felony (first); Class 4 Felony (repeat or in violation of protection order)
elements: Defendant knowingly engaged in a course of conduct directed at a specific person
Would cause a reasonable person to suffer serious emotional distress
The defendant knew or should have known the conduct would cause the victim to suffer
enhancements: In violation of a protection order (Class 4 Felony)
notes: Stalking is always a felony in Colorado. Making a credible threat elevates to Class 4 Felony.

elements: Defendant with intent to harass, annoy, or alarm another person
Struck, shoved, kicked, or touched another person
Or directed obscene language or gestures to another in a public place
Or followed another in a public place
notes: Bias-motivated harassment (based on race, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, disability, sexual orientation, or gender identity) is enhanced to Class 1 Misdemeanor.

statute_title: Crimes Against At-Risk Adults and At-Risk Juveniles
offense_class: Enhanced one class above the underlying offense
penalty_max: Varies — one class above underlying offense
fine_max: Varies — one class above underlying offense
elements: Defendant committed a crime against an at-risk person
At-risk person includes those 70+ or those unable to protect themselves due to disability
Or a person in the care of a facility
notes: Colorado enhances crimes against at-risk adults and juveniles by one felony/misdemeanor class. At-risk includes adults 70+ and those with disabilities.

statute_title: Possession of Weapons by Previous Offenders
offense_class: Class 5 Felony (non-violent prior); Class 4 Felony (violent prior)
elements: Defendant possessed, used, or carried a firearm
Defendant had a prior felony conviction or was otherwise prohibited
notes: Colorado prohibits firearm possession by convicted felons, those subject to protection orders, and those adjudicated mentally defective.

statute_title: Possession of a Weapon by a Previous Offender
offense_class: Class 5 Felony (non-violent prior); Class 4 Felony (violent prior)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed a firearm
Defendant had been convicted of a felony
Or defendant had been convicted of a misdemeanor domestic violence offense
notes: Applies to all convicted felons and domestic violence misdemeanants. Prior violent felony elevates from Class 5 to Class 4 Felony.

elements: Defendant knowingly and unlawfully carried a concealed weapon
Without a valid concealed handgun permit
Not on own property
notes: Colorado requires a concealed handgun permit. First offense is a Class 2 Misdemeanor. Subsequent offenses are Class 5 Felonies.

elements: Defendant knowingly or recklessly discharged a firearm
Into a dwelling or occupied building
Or in a manner that created a grave risk of death or serious bodily injury
notes: Also covered by reckless endangerment (§ 18-3-208). Firing into an occupied building carries additional enhancement risk.

elements: Defendant knowingly used the personal identifying information of another
Without authorization or permission
To obtain anything of value, credit, or a financial instrument
notes: Class 4 Felony. Enhanced when targeting at-risk adults (70+). Mandatory restitution.

offense_class: Same as theft by degree based on value
penalty_max: Same as theft by value tier
fine_max: Same as theft by value tier
elements: Defendant was entrusted with property of another
Defendant knowingly obtained or exercised unauthorized control over the property
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: Charged under the general theft statute. Embezzlement is a theory of theft, not a separate crime.

elements: Defendant with intent to defraud
Falsely made, completed, altered, or uttered a written instrument
Which is or purports to be a document of legal significance
notes: Forgery is a Class 5 Felony regardless of the type of document. Covers government documents, financial instruments, deeds, wills, and contracts.

statute_title: Criminal Possession of a Forged Instrument
elements: Defendant possessed a forged instrument
With knowledge that it was forged
With intent to defraud
notes: Counterfeiting of currency is primarily federal. State charges typically involve forged documents.

offense_class: Petty Offense (under $300); Class 2 Misdemeanor ($300-$750); escalates by value tier
penalty_max: Same as theft by value tier
fine_max: Same as theft by value tier
elements: Defendant issued a check, draft, or order for payment of money
Knowing there were insufficient funds
With intent to defraud
notes: Classified by amount using the same value tiers as theft.

elements: Defendant made a false, incomplete, or misleading statement
In connection with an insurance claim or application
With intent to defraud an insurer
notes: Includes filing false claims, staged accidents, and arson-for-profit. Mandatory restitution.

statute_title: Criminal Possession or Use of Financial Transaction Device
elements: Defendant used a credit card, debit card, or financial transaction device
Knowing it was stolen, forged, revoked, or canceled
With intent to defraud
notes: Colorado uses 'financial transaction device' to cover credit cards, debit cards, and similar instruments.

elements: Defendant conducted or attempted to conduct a financial transaction
Involving proceeds of specified unlawful activity
With knowledge that the transaction was designed to conceal or disguise the nature or source of the proceeds
notes: Class 3 Felony. Colorado also has structuring provisions to prevent evasion of reporting requirements.

offense_class: Same as theft by degree based on value
elements: Defendant obtained property by deception
Created or confirmed a false impression of fact
With intent to permanently deprive the owner
notes: General fraud charged under the theft statute as theft by deception.

offense_class: Class 4 Felony (basic); Class 3 Felony (with force or weapon); Class 2 Felony (involving serious bodily injury)
elements: Defendant knowingly inflicted sexual intrusion or penetration on a victim
Through the use of force, intimidation, or coercion
Or the victim was physically helpless or incapable of consent
mandatory_minimum: Indeterminate sentence to DOC possible under lifetime supervision provisions
enhancements: Use of force or weapon (Class 3 Felony)
notes: Colorado uses 'sexual assault' broadly. Indeterminate sentencing may apply. Sex offender registration required. No statute of limitations.

elements: Defendant knowingly inflicted sexual intrusion or penetration on a victim
By use of physical force, violence, or physical helplessness
Without consent
notes: Colorado eliminated the term 'rape' from its statutes in 2000. All penetration offenses are 'sexual assault.' Indeterminate sentencing allows for lifetime supervision.

elements: Defendant knowingly exposed their genitals to the view of any person
Under circumstances in which the defendant knew the conduct was likely to cause affront or alarm
enhancements: Exposure to a child (may trigger sex offense charges)
notes: First offense is Class 1 Misdemeanor. Subsequent offenses become a Class 6 Felony and may require sex offender registration.

elements: Defendant offered to perform or performed an act of prostitution
Or solicited another to patronize a prostitute
enhancements: Solicitation involving a minor (enhanced felony charges)
notes: Both the person offering and the patron can be charged. Patronizing a prostituted child (§ 18-7-406) is a Class 3 Felony.

offense_class: Class 3 Felony (possession of 20+); Class 4 Felony (possession under 20); Class 3 Felony (distribution)
elements: Defendant knowingly possessed, produced, or distributed material depicting a child engaged in sexually explicit conduct
Defendant knew or should have known the subject was a child
notes: Federal charges are common in addition to state charges. Sex offender registration required. Indeterminate sentencing may apply.

statute_title: Failure to Register as a Sex Offender
elements: Defendant was required to register under the Colorado Sex Offender Registration Act
Defendant knowingly failed to register or update registration as required
notes: Must register within 5 business days. Colorado Sex Offender Registration Act requires registration for varying periods depending on offense.

offense_class: Class 4 Felony (victim 15-16, defendant 10+ years older); Class 3 Felony (victim under 15, under § 18-3-405)
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual contact or penetration with a child
Victim was under the age of 17 (age of consent)
Defendant was 10 or more years older than the victim (for ages 15-16)
notes: Age of consent in Colorado is 17 (15-16 with partner less than 10 years older). Sexual assault on a child (§ 18-3-405) covers victims under 15. Sex offender registration required.

offense_class: Class 1 Petty Offense (basic); Class 2 Misdemeanor (discharge of firearm)
elements: Defendant made a coarse and obviously offensive utterance, gesture, or display in a public place
Or abused or threatened a person in a public place
Tending to incite an immediate breach of the peace
notes: Basic disorderly conduct is a petty offense. Disorderly conduct involving discharge of a firearm is a Class 2 Misdemeanor.

elements: Defendant knowingly prevented or attempted to prevent a peace officer
Acting under color of official authority
From effecting an arrest of the defendant or another
By using or threatening to use physical force or violence
enhancements: Use of physical force causing injury (additional assault charges)
notes: It is not a defense that the arrest was unlawful. Physical resistance causing injury may lead to additional assault charges.

elements: Defendant knowingly obstructed, impaired, or hindered
The enforcement of the penal law or the preservation of the peace
By a peace officer acting under color of official authority
notes: Broader than resisting arrest — covers interference with any law enforcement activity.

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor (indirect criminal contempt); varies for direct
elements: Defendant willfully disobeyed a lawful order of the court
Or engaged in disruptive behavior in the courtroom
Or failed to appear as ordered
notes: Criminal contempt is punitive; civil contempt is coercive. Right to jury trial for serious criminal contempt.

elements: Person is found in a public place under the influence of alcohol or drugs
To the degree that the person is incapacitated
notes: Colorado decriminalized public intoxication. Intoxicated persons may be taken to a detox facility rather than jail. No criminal penalty applies. Local ordinances may vary.

offense_class: Class 6 Felony (felony case); Class 2 Misdemeanor (misdemeanor case)
elements: Defendant was released on bail or personal recognizance
Required to appear at a specified time and place
Defendant knowingly failed to appear as required
notes: Bench warrant issued upon failure to appear. Bond forfeiture in addition to criminal charges.

offense_class: Class 2 Misdemeanor (basic); Class 1 Misdemeanor (false emergency report)
elements: Defendant reported false information to a law enforcement agency
Knowing the information to be false
Regarding a crime or emergency
notes: False emergency reports (bomb threats, active shooter, swatting) are Class 1 Misdemeanor.

offense_class: Class 3 Misdemeanor (basic); Class 5 Felony (with deadly weapon)
elements: Defendant by physical action or threat knowingly placed or attempted to place another person
In fear of imminent serious bodily injury
enhancements: Use or display of a deadly weapon (Class 5 Felony)
notes: Colorado uses 'menacing' rather than 'criminal threat' or 'terroristic threat.' Menacing with a deadly weapon is a Class 5 Felony.

elements: Defendant made a materially false statement under oath
In or in connection with an official proceeding
Defendant did not believe the statement to be true
notes: First-degree perjury in an official proceeding is a Class 4 Felony. Second-degree (§ 18-8-503) covers other sworn statements (Class 1 Misdemeanor).

elements: Defendant offered, conferred, or agreed to confer any benefit
Upon a public servant
With intent to influence the public servant's official action
notes: Both the giver and receiver can be charged. Receiving a bribe (§ 18-8-303) is also a Class 3 Felony.

offense_class: Class 2 Felony (from custody for Class 1/2/3 Felony); Class 4 Felony (from other felony custody); Class 2 Misdemeanor (from misdemeanor custody)
elements: Defendant escaped or attempted to escape from custody or confinement
Defendant was in lawful custody
enhancements: Use of force or deadly weapon
notes: Severity depends on the underlying offense. Escape from custody for a serious felony is itself a serious felony.

offense_class: Class 1 Misdemeanor (basic); Class 6 Felony (aggravated, first); Class 5 Felony (aggravated, second+)
elements: Defendant knowingly, recklessly, or with criminal negligence
Overdrove, overloaded, overworked, tortured, tormented, or needlessly mutilated an animal
Or failed to provide adequate food, water, shelter, or protection
notes: Colorado enhanced animal cruelty penalties significantly. Aggravated cruelty to animals involving torture is a Class 6 Felony. Animal fighting is a Class 5 Felony.

penalty_max: Remaining suspended sentence on underlying offense
elements: Defendant was placed on probation
Defendant violated a condition of probation
Violation was established at a revocation hearing
enhancements: New criminal offense while on probation
notes: Judge has discretion to revoke, modify, or continue probation. Defendant entitled to a revocation hearing. Graduated sanctions may apply for technical violations.

penalty_max: Return to DOC for remaining sentence
elements: Defendant was released on parole
Defendant violated a condition of parole
Violation was established at a revocation hearing
notes: Colorado Parole Board makes revocation decisions. Technical violations may result in graduated sanctions. Community return-to-custody facilities may be used.

elements: Defendant aided, abetted, advised, or encouraged another person
In the planning or commission of an offense
With the intent to promote or facilitate the commission of the offense
notes: A complicitor is legally accountable for the behavior of another and is punishable as a principal.

offense_class: One class below the attempted offense; attempt of Class 1 Felony is Class 2 Felony
penalty_max: Varies by class of the attempted offense
fine_max: Varies by class of the attempted offense
elements: Defendant acting with the kind of culpability otherwise required for commission of an offense
Engaged in conduct constituting a substantial step toward the commission of the offense
notes: Attempt reduces the offense classification by one level. Attempt of a Class 1 Felony is a Class 2 Felony.

offense_class: One class below the target offense
penalty_max: Varies by class of target offense
fine_max: Varies by class of target offense
elements: Defendant agreed with one or more persons that they or one of them would engage in conduct which constitutes a crime
Defendant or a co-conspirator committed an overt act in pursuance of the conspiracy
With the intent to promote or facilitate the commission of the crime
notes: Conspiracy is one level below the target offense. Requires an overt act. Renunciation is an affirmative defense.
